annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Canal Zone (8)' for PANORAMA: PANAMA (canal) round OR would fit, but no clue word gives OR or defines the answer; the clue looks cut short and no scan or search gives the rest.

clue.text: I enter political group on equal terms

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for the noun state of being equal

indicators.note: to enter something is to go into it, so the letter goes inside the group

parts.note: a party is a political group

explanation.surface: A newcomer joins a political faction and is treated as an equal.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is equality of status, the condition of standing level with others.

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: Someone catches a girl further down the slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or beneath, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: Gathering at church to repent outwardly

indicators.note: the word for repent is placed on the outside, wrapping the abbreviation for church

parts.note: to rue is to regret or repent

explanation.surface: At a church meeting, people show penitence in public.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a gathered strip of fabric used as a frill or trim.

indicators.note: one piece is placed straight after, on the end of, the other

parts.note: etc. means 'and so on', giving the letters S, O, O, N

explanation.surface: A breeze blows on Monday and the days that follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'etc.' stands for 'and so on'; drop the 'and' to get SO ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A monsoon is a seasonal wind of South Asia bringing heavy rain.

parts.note: Tom is a boy's name, and two boys give it twice
the second boy is another Tom

explanation.surface: Some lads are playing a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a hand-beaten drum of tribal origin.

clue.text: It's a mistake to give short change

definitions.text: It's a mistake to give short change

parts.words: It's a mistake to give short change
parts.note: a shopkeeper who hands back too little money has usually just failed to notice, a slip of attention rather than a fraud

explanation.surface: A cashier is told that short-changing customers is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is an unintentional failure to notice something, an error by omission.

clue.text: Relating to the subject of the act I'm rewriting

indicators.note: rewriting a text recasts it, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A lawyer reworks a statute to fit the topic in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Thematic means concerning a theme, the topic of a work.

clue.text: State to find the king in

definitions.text: State to find the king in

parts.words: State to find the king in
parts.note: reads like a question about where the king is, but describes a kind of nation headed by a crowned ruler

explanation.surface: Someone asks which country holds the missing king.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchy is a country ruled by a sovereign such as a king or queen.

clue.text: Again model has a very small amount of money reserved

parts.note: RE is a prefix meaning again
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so T stands for model
a means one, the Roman numeral I
a cent is a coin of very low value

explanation.surface: A fashion model, back again, has little cash left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' only joins; the T comes from the Ford Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person is reticent, holding back from speaking freely.

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the churchman's letters surround the other word

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vicar on a lower step hugs the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to degrade them, to bring their standing down.

clue.text: Not a cheap term of affection

definitions.meaning: a loving form of address like darling

explanation.surface: Endearments that come at a price.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: costly in price, and a fond way of addressing a loved one.

clue.text: For this reason the said number of soldiers were included

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed within the letters of the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: said marks a word spoken, so the number is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: four is a number
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Logic explains why that many soldiers joined up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' tells you to swap the number for a word that sounds like it, and 'were included' puts the Royal Engineers inside; 'of' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore is a connective meaning consequently, introducing a conclusion.

parts.note: reads as an invitation to come in, but describes one tread of an indoor flight between floors

explanation.surface: A host invites a visitor in.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is one of the steps on an indoor staircase.

definitions.meaning: one's life ... is the length of a life
the ... of a bridge is the part between supports

explanation.surface: A whole life devoted to a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a stretch of time and the arch of a bridge between piers.

parts.note: plain means clear, obvious
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone in court makes a plainly stated case.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who brings a lawsuit, one kind of litigant.

indicators.note: ragged means torn and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A scruffy rascal is coarse and unkempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Roguish means mischievous in the manner of a rogue or scamp.

clue.text: But is of practical significance to a university teacher

definitions.text: But is of practical significance to a university teacher

parts.words: But is of practical significance to a university teacher
parts.note: the word means of no practical significance, theoretical, yet it is also what a university lecturer is, so it matters in practice to one

explanation.surface: A point dismissed as theoretical still matters to a lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic means both purely theoretical and, as a noun, a university scholar.

parts.note: an impost is a tax or duty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between paying duty and committing fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: An impostor is someone who deceives by pretending to be another person.

definitions.meaning: a pact or treaty between parties

explanation.surface: A deal that has only limited support.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: closely packed together, and a formal pact between states.

clue.text: The first to enquire about the amount of work set

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word The is taken

parts.note: to ask is to enquire

explanation.surface: Someone is first to ask how much homework there is.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work assigned to someone.

definitions.meaning: to judge the worth of, assess

explanation.surface: Guess how fast something is going.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to assess or value, and a measure of pace.

indicators.note: a word that can be read in two directions, forwards and backwards, giving the same letters

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A drink that works both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviver is a restorative drink, something that refreshes you.

clue.text: A great amount is not mentioned

explanation.surface: Huge sums are kept quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: beyond counting, as in untold riches, and never spoken or related.

clue.text: Church caretaker right on the brink

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece is put on top of another; here the brink comes before right

parts.note: the verge is the edge or brink

explanation.surface: A church official is on the edge of being right.
explanation.definitionFit: A verger is a church official who looks after the building and leads processions.

indicators.note: the first letter goes into the word for feathers

parts.note: down is soft fine plumage

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of revolutionary is used

explanation.surface: A rebel chief is plunged into a pile of feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown something is to submerge or flood it completely.

definitions.meaning: the money paid on leaving a job

explanation.surface: A pay cut of some kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Severance pay is redundancy money; severance is also the act of cutting off.

explanation.surface: Sharing the bills between flatmates.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: tears in fabric, and money paid regularly by a tenant.

indicators.note: freely means without restraint, so these letters are rearranged at will

explanation.surface: Blend tar loosely into a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: A matrix is a mould in which something is cast or shaped.

parts.note: even means level, plain
a song is a chant

explanation.surface: Simple singing in a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is evening prayer, a sung service in the Anglican church.

clue.text: Artilleryman in the restaurant has a bottle

indicators.note: the soldier sits within the eating place

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant
RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for a gunner

explanation.surface: A gunner in a bistro is holding a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass bottle for serving wine or water at table.

clue.text: Protester more unprepared about South Africa

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: cruder means rougher, less refined or prepared

explanation.surface: An activist is even less prepared regarding South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader is a campaigner who fights vigorously for a cause.
